interest: Hutchison's candid doubts that Chiang's government could carry out agricultural reform, plus the full commission roster.
overview: 1946 correspondence on the Chinese-American Agricultural Collaboration Commission, including Dean Claude B. Hutchison's progress report to President Truman and his doubts about Chinese reform.

subfiles.about: Reports on arrangements with Edwin A. Locke, Jr. for State Department representation during the agricultural mission's upcoming White House visit.
subfiles.from: Arthur R. Ringwalt (Division of Chinese Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Ringwalt tells Vincent that Locke agreed a Benton or FE representative should attend the agricultural mission's White House visit.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Ringwalt to Vincent regarding White House Visit of Agricultural Mission
subfiles.to: John Carter Vincent (Office of Far Eastern Affairs)

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of letters from Dean Claude B. Hutchison addressed to President Truman and Edwin A. Locke, Jr.
subfiles.from: R. E. Moore (Chief, Technical Collaboration Branch, OFAR, USDA)
subfiles.summary: R. E. Moore of USDA sends Ringwalt copies of Hutchison's October 28, 1946 letters to Truman and Locke.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Moore to Ringwalt Transmitting Hutchison Letters
subfiles.to: Arthur R. Ringwalt (Department of State, Office of Far Eastern Affairs)

subfiles.about: Transmits a progress letter for President Truman and comments on the difficult agricultural conditions facing China's National Government.
subfiles.from: Claude Burton Hutchison (Head, American Section, Chinese-American Agricultural Collaboration Commission)
subfiles.summary: Hutchison sends Locke his report for Truman from Nanking, frankly questioning whether the National Government can carry out needed agricultural measures.
subfiles.title: Letter from Hutchison to Locke Transmitting Report to President Truman
subfiles.to: Edwin A. Locke, Jr. (Special Assistant to the President)

subfiles.about: Reports to President Truman on the mission's reception, field work in China, proposed collaborative projects, and scheduled return to Washington.
subfiles.from: Claude Burton Hutchison (Head, American Section, Chinese-American Agricultural Collaboration Commission)
subfiles.summary: Hutchison reports to Truman on the ten-member agricultural mission's reception in China by Chiang Kai-shek and T. V. Soong, stresses agriculture's central role, and plans to return about November 22.
subfiles.title: Letter from Hutchison to President Truman on Agricultural Mission to China
